 “Dragon Ball Super: Beerus” 1×01 and 1×02 Review – “The God Who Destroys”
 October 20, 2026 
 Farid-ul-Haq 
 Super Saiyan 3 Goku vs Beerus (Image via Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Anime Season 1 Episode 2) 
 Dragon Ball Super: Beerus anime season 1 episode 1, titled ‘The God Who Destroys’, and episode 2, The God of Destruction Heads to the Planet of the Kai’, gave fans a very good idea of what to expect from this retelling of the OG Dragon Ball Super anime.
 I shared my initial opinions about Dragon Ball Super: Beerus after watching the trailer back in September . As someone who (in a manner) keeps up with the Dragon Ball IP, I would have much preferred an anime adapting new storylines from the manga instead of going back to Dragon Ball Super and giving it a fresh coat of animation. However, having seen the first two episodes of DBS: Beerus , I have to say that I enjoyed the current anime offering for a number of reasons.
 One of the most fun things about DBS: Beerus , for me, was the pacing. This particular retelling didn’t spend time going over the so-called filler content from the OG anime. The first two episodes were full of action while giving enough time to character motivations to set up the current conflict involving Beerus. And you know what? I’m here for it. 
 Certain anime are infamous for dragging out plotlines, fight sequences, and featuring filler to meet weekly episode counts. The OG DBS anime was one such property. That’s also why I thought DBS: Beerus would stick to the original’s pacing. Fortunately, it didn’t. And that immediately boosted my interest in it.
 ‘The God Who Destroys’ quickly gave viewers a rundown of where Goku and his family were four years after the crew’s battle with Majin Buu. Goku had taken up farming to earn money. Even though he wanted to continue training, Goku had enough sense to keep his priorities in order after Chi-Chi told him how his household required financial support. 
 Even though the fandom jokes about Goku being an absent father, the actual story does a lot to showcase how much Goku loves his family. Yes, he wants to train to become stronger, but his training sessions will take a backseat when it comes to being present for his wife and kids. Of course, the plot found a way to make Chi-Chi permit Goku to go off-planet to train properly, but the fact remained that Goku didn’t even try to leave until he ensured his family would be financially provided for.
 The scene where Goku trained by himself during his lunch break by mentally sparring against Frieza, Cell, and Kid Buu made for a nice action sequence to highlight the anime’s animation quality compared to the OG.
 As for Vegeta, he was also busy training inside one of Bulma’s gravity domes. Understandably, Vegeta’s motivation continued to be him wanting to not only grow stronger than before, but to surpass Goku as the most powerful Saiyan ever.
 Coming to Beerus’s introduction, the God of Destruction finally woke up after a 39-year-long nap. Beerus’s characterization was quite simple. He just enjoyed destroying planets, mostly on a whim. We got to see him destroy half a planet because he thought a particular dessert had too much fat in it. Beerus then proceeded to destroy an entire planet because a clan’s chief refused to hand over a dinosaur that Beerus wanted to taste.
 Even though one could argue about Beerus’ moral code, I don’t have much to say about him because I know the type of character development Beerus will go through. As of right now, Beerus is very arrogant and that’s not going to change anytime soon.
 Episode 2, ‘The God of Destruction Heads to the Planet of the Kai’, was about layering the lore around Beerus, which I appreciated. Old Kai and King Kai sensed Beerus waking up. They already knew about the God of Destruction and were hoping Beerus didn’t set his sights on Earth. Not only that, but they also hoped Goku didn’t learn about Beerus, because knowing Goku, he won’t be able to prevent himself from asking Beerus to a match.
 More backstory involved Beerus having ordered Frieza to destroy the Saiyans because they annoyed Beerus. This particular detail gave Beerus a very strong connection to both Vegeta and Goku, even before they had met. I’m looking forward to seeing how both Saiyans will react after learning that Beerus was the reason their people were attacked.
 Fate was also in play, with there being a prophecy about Beerus facing off against a being called a Super Saiyan God. So, even though the storyline could be chalked up to plot convenience, the writers still managed to make Beerus’ journey to Earth feel organic. Beerus didn’t just teleport to Earth. He first stopped at King Kai’s planet while trying to collect more information about the mysterious Super Saiyan God. Though arrogant, I liked how the writers made Beerus put in some detective work to quench his curiosity. 
 Beerus’s arrival on King Kai’s planet is what led him to meet Goku. It was funny seeing King Kai try to hide Goku inside his house from a freaking God of Destruction. There was no way Goku could have suppressed his Ki to make himself invisible to Beerus.
 Staying true to character, Goku asked Beerus to a sparring match after answering that he had never heard of a Super Saiyan God. Beerus blowing up planets with a snap of his fingers had shown us his power. But seeing Goku struggle against Beerus just hit different. Goku unleashed Super Saiyan 1, Super Saiyan 2, and even Super Saiyan 3. Yet he wasn’t able to land a single hit on Beerus. 
 My favorite moment was how Goku instinctively backed away from Beerus just because Beerus had decided to finally attack Goku. Even though our lead couldn’t sense a God’s Ki, his instincts still kicked in to keep him on the defensive. It was clear that Goku was fighting a being his past opponents didn’t compare to.
 After knocking out Goku with a single hit, Beerus and Whis set off to Earth. Such a defeat is going to motivate Goku to find a way to get stronger. I’m looking forward to seeing Beerus ask Vegeta about a Super Saiyan God and Vegeta’s reaction to realizing that Beerus was aware of the Saiyan Prince. Vegeta will be humbled, but I’m so excited for the high-quality action! 
 Did you watch Dragon Ball Super: Beerus anime season 1 episodes 1 and 2? What did you think of them?
